data.title: Middle East Eye: Green Party recognises Zionism as a form of racism and backs single Palestinian state
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Green Party recognises Zionism as a form of racism and backs single Palestinian state
The Green Party of England and Wales has voted to declare Zionism a form of racism in an unprecedented move at its party conference in Brighton, Middle East Eye has learnt.
The vote by party members on Sunday makes it the first major party in the UK to recognise Zionism as a form of racism - and to back a single democratic Palestinian state with equal rights for all ethnic and religious groups, rather than a two-state solution.
1,022 members voted for the motion while 813 voted against it.
Co-Deputy Leader Mothin Ali told Middle East Eye on Sunday that he was strongly in favour of the motion, unlike Green MPs Carla Denyer and Adrian Ramsay, who criticised it.
"As defined in the motion," Ali said, "Zionism is an ethno-nationalist state. Zionism is resulting in ethnic cleansing, in the belief that one group of people is superior to another."

data.title: Middle East Eye: ‘The Israeli occupation does not distinguish’: Gaza family mourns Christian mother and daughter
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
‘The Israeli occupation does not distinguish’: Gaza family mourns Christian mother and daughter
Fourteen-year-old Fuad woke up at around 5am on Saturday at his father’s house to get ready for school.
He learned that his mother and grandmother had been killed in an Israeli air strike on their apartment in western Gaza City.
Mary Abu Dawud and her mother Maysaa were among the five Palestinians killed in the al-Asala residential building, after three strikes hit the area at around 1.30am, according to Palestinian authorities and church representatives.
“My mother was thrown against the wall by the force of the explosion, and my grandmother was engulfed in flames after the missile hit the house,” Fuad said.
“Today, I lost the most precious person in my life. There are no words to describe my feelings.”

data.title: Middle East Eye: Over 70 dead in fighting around Yemen's Taiz in 24 hours
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Over 70 dead in fighting around Yemen's Taiz in 24 hours
More than 70 people have been killed over the past day in fighting in and around the southwestern Yemeni province of Taiz, AFP reported on Sunday, citing sources from both sides.
Sources from the Yemeni government reported that 34 troops were killed, 20 of them in neighbouring Lahj, on the edge of Taiz province.
Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in areas bordering Lahj.
The Yemeni government announced earlier on Sunday that it had launched a new wave of military operations to reclaim Houthi-controlled territory.
The same day, the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking Taiz with Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised government.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran airlines resume flights to Iraq’s Najaf after US exemption
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Iran airlines resume flights to Iraq’s Najaf after US exemption
Iranian airlines resumed flights to Iraq’s Najaf on Sunday after the United States granted Baghdad an exemption allowing sanctioned Iranian carriers to operate to the city holy to Shia Muslims, AFP reported.
On Friday, the Iraqi government said it had secured an agreement with the US allowing Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate 40 daily flights to and from Najaf.
Last month, Iraq enforced the US ban on Iranian carriers, especially at Najaf’s airport, which is a major hub for Iranian flights.
The US also granted Iraqi Airways, the national carrier, a waiver to fly between Najaf and Iran, with the flights expected to start this month.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Netanyahu orders security review of international flights to Israel after Flydubai incident
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Netanyahu orders security review of international flights to Israel after Flydubai incident
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday ordered a security review of international flights to Israel after a co-pilot allegedly attempted to crash an Israel-bound flight from Dubai.
Netanyahu "has instructed the Head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel", a statement from his office said.
The Israel-bound Flydubai flight made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on 30 September after its Omani co-pilot allegedly attempted to crash the plane, which was carrying 180 passengers, most of them Israeli.
Netanyahu said on Friday that Israel was examining whether anyone had directed the co-pilot, vowing a "heavy price" for those involved.
A source close to the UAE government accused the Israeli government of exploiting the incident for political purposes, Israeli media reported on Saturday.

One killed, over 15 wounded by Israeli forces and settlers in West Bank
Israeli violence continued to escalate across the occupied West Bank on Sunday.
More than 15 people were wounded and one person was killed in attacks by Israeli forces and settlers on Palestinian towns and villages, the Wafa news agency reported.
Earlier in the day, a Palestinian man had been killed by Israeli soldiers while being detained at the Anab checkpoint, east of Tulkarm.
In Beit Imrin, northwest of Nablus, Israeli troops beat and injured four Palestinian men.
The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its medics treated the four and took them to hospital.
In Sebastia, another town in the northwest of Nablus, Israeli settlers beat a 45-year-old Palestinian man, leaving him with bruises and wounds, Wafa reported.
Settlers blocked ambulance crews from reaching him.
Israel will close all crossings in the occupied West Bank from 5 to 7 October for the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.

Iranian oil minister steps down
Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, the president's office said in a statement on Sunday, amid long queues at petrol stations caused by the ongoing war and US sanctions.
Government spokesperson Mehdi Tabatabaei told state TV later on Sunday that Paknejad, a member of President Pezeshkian's cabinet since August 2024, resigned for personal reasons "a long time ago."
Hamid Bord, the CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), "has been appointed as acting Minister of Oil by a decree from the president", according to a statement carried by Iran’s state media.
Bord has held senior positions at NIOC and previously headed several of its operating units, including the National Iranian South Oil Company and the Iranian Offshore Oil Company.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel shells Syria's Quneitra while Qatar and Jordan condemn its excavation near occupied Golan
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israel shells Syria's Quneitra while Qatar and Jordan condemn its excavation near occupied Golan
Israeli forces shelled farmland between Buraiqa and Kodana in southern Quneitra, Syria's Al-Ikhbariah TV reported on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Syria, Qatar and Jordan denounced Israel's resumed construction on the "Sofa 53" project in Syria's Quneitra province.
The project, also called the "Great Storm", is a military road that Israel began building in 2022 within the buffer zone established under the 1974 disengagement agreement.
It stretches from northern Quneitra down towards the meeting point of the Syrian, Jordanian and Israeli borders.
Syria's Foreign Ministry said on Sunday that Israel's resumption of excavation work near the separation line with the occupied Syrian Golan Heights was a "flagrant breach" of the 1974 deal.
Qatar also described the project as a violation of Syrian sovereignty and international law and a threat to stability in the region.
Jordan expressed similar condemnation, with foreign ministry spokesperson Fuad Majali urging Israel to stop all actions targeting Syria.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli opposition leader calls for Jordanian-Israeli control over West Bank
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israeli opposition leader calls for Jordanian-Israeli control over West Bank
Israeli opposition leader Avigdor Lieberman on Sunday called for the Palestinian Authority (PA) to be dismantled and for an Israeli-Jordanian confederation to control parts of the West Bank currently under the PA's control, according to Haaretz.
Lieberman, chairman of the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party, presented a plan titled "Israel's Endgame in the West Bank and Gaza".
Under it, Israel would apply sovereignty over Area C, which makes up about 60 percent of the occupied West Bank and remains under full Israeli control.
The plan proposes an Israeli-Jordanian confederation in Areas A and B, where the PA exercises limited control.
Jordan would run civilian affairs and policing there, while Israel would keep "full security responsibility" across the entire territory, according to Lieberman's plan.
He also called for control of the Gaza Strip to be handed to an "external party", which he did not specify.
Under international law, the entire territory covering Areas A, B and C is Palestinian land and all Israeli settlements on them are illegal. The vast majority of Israel’s 700,000 settlers live illegally in Area C.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel slams Green Party after members vote to define Zionism as racism
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israel slams Green Party after members vote to define Zionism as racism
Israel has accused the Green Party of England and Wales of giving "legitimacy to terrorism" after its members voted on Sunday to recognise Zionism as a form of racism.
The vote makes the Greens the first major UK party to define Zionism as racism and to back a single democratic Palestinian state with equal rights for all ethnic and religious groups, rather than a two-state solution.
Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the new policy went "far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate" and called on other British parties to condemn the resolution.
"The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle," the ministry wrote on social media.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog called the move "a disgrace and a shame".
"Those who claim the antisemitic lie that 'Zionism is racism' deliberately endanger Jews and Israelis everywhere," he wrote on social media.

In a separate statement, the Israeli army also claimed that it had killed a commander of Hamas's armed wing in another strike in the same area.

No military solution to US-Iran war, Iranian foreign minister says
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States’ war against the Islamic Republic, with talks on ending the war between the two countries apparently at an impasse.
“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Lebanon seeks 'new chapter' with Iran, prime minister says
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Lebanon seeks 'new chapter' with Iran, prime minister says
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Sunday that Lebanon wants a new chapter in relations with Iran based on mutual respect and non-interference.
In an interview with Lebanese broadcaster NBN, Salam stated that he had accepted a meeting requested by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, saying: "We do not interfere in Iran's affairs."
He said Lebanon would prefer Iran to appoint a new ambassador, noting that the current envoy's residence permit had been renewed for three months "as a citizen" but not in his previous diplomatic capacity.
Salam also said Lebanon cannot "sit and wait" for a settlement between the US and Iran.
"If it happens, that's good. And if it doesn't happen, are we to remain sitting and waiting?" he said.
"The state cannot remain in a state of waiting. We must head south and to all regions and bear our responsibilities."
He added that "not a day passes" without Lebanon reaffirming its demand for a full Israeli withdrawal, along with an end to Israeli attacks, a firmer ceasefire and the release of prisoners.

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Election panel orders Netanyahu to remove 'election propaganda' videos
The chairman of Israel's Central Elections Committee chairman ordered that prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu remove online videos where military and public resources were used without authorisation, according to Haaretz.
With election season in Israel set to begin on 27 October, Noam Sohlberg ruled that the videos constituted campaigning and included remarks that could only be seen as "boasting" over the government and the prime minister's achievements.
He also said that the videos are "election propaganda whose intention is to persuade the voter", and ordered Netanyahu to also pay the petitioners 29,000 shekels ($9,500) in legal fees.
